The Boondocks (2010)

The Boondocks is a satirical animated series (based on Aaron McGruder’s comic strip) that follows the Freeman family—10-year-old revolutionary Huey, his 8-year-old brother Riley, and their grandfather Robert—after moving from Chicago to the quiet, predominantly white suburb of Woodcrest. It explores race, politics, and culture through sharp comedy.

source_details.synopsis: The Boondocks is an American adult animated black sitcom created by Aaron McGruder for Cartoon Network's late-night programming block Adult Swim, based on his manga-influenced comic strip of the same name. The series focuses on a Black American family, the Freemans, and their experiences in the fictional, predominantly white suburb of Woodcrest. The perspective offered by this mixture of cultures, lifestyles, social classes, stereotypes, viewpoints and racialized identities provides for much of the series' satire, comedy, and conflict.
